transcript.text: My Miele dryer takes ages now and keeps flashing a filter warning even though I clean the fluff filter in the door every time. Is it on its way out?

Probably not on its way out. That warning means the dryer is detecting restricted airflow, and slow drying is the classic knock-on effect. Cleaning the door filter is the right habit, but on most Miele dryers (especially heat-pump ones) it isn't the only filter, and the other one is the usual culprit when the warning won't clear. Most likely causes, in order:
1. A clogged plinth filter or heat exchanger behind the flap at the bottom front.
2. Door filters that look clean but have a fine film of lint or fabric conditioner blocking the mesh.
3. If yours is a vented model, a kinked or fluffed-up vent hose. Checks, with the dryer switched off and unplugged:
1. Open the flap at the bottom front and pull out the sponge (plinth) filter. If it's matted with fluff, rinse it under the tap, squeeze it out, and let it dry or refit it slightly damp. While it's out, look at the fins behind it. If they're furred with lint, rinse them gently with the shower head or a soft brush (the manual shows how), taking care not to bend them. A clogged one here would explain both the warning and the long cycles.
2. Take the door filters out (there are often two parts, upper and lower) and wash them under warm running water, not just wiped. Hold them up to the light. If water beads on the mesh or you can't see through it, scrub gently with a soft brush and a little washing-up liquid to remove the conditioner film. Check for tears too.
3. If it's a vented model, check the hose out of the back is short, unkinked and clear. After cleaning, run a normal programme with a normal load (no more than about two-thirds full and well spun). On a heat-pump dryer, a longer cycle than an old-style dryer is normal. The warning flashing every time, though, is not. If the warning keeps coming back with every filter and the heat exchanger properly clean, that points to an airflow sensing or fan problem inside the machine. That's an engineer job, and Miele's own service is worth considering. Is there a sponge filter behind a bottom flap on yours, and was it furred up?

I didn't know there was a second filter, but yes, it was behind the bottom flap and completely matted with fluff. The fins behind it had a felt-like layer of fluff too, which I vacuumed off gently. I've since run a normal load and it dried in just over 2 hours with no warning. There's no burning smell, just the normal hum. Is that all it needed?

Yes, by the sound of it that was all it needed. A completely matted plinth filter plus a felted layer on the heat exchanger fins would choke the airflow badly, which is exactly what triggers the filter warning and drags the cycle out. Drying a normal load in just over two hours with no warning, a normal hum and no burning smell is a healthy result, so there's no sign it's on its way out. To stop it happening again:
1. Keep cleaning the door filters after every load, and give them a proper rinse under warm water every few weeks so fabric conditioner film doesn't build up on the mesh.
2. Check the plinth sponge filter roughly every month or so (more often if you dry a lot of towels or fleece), rinse it when it looks grey or furry, and glance at the fins behind it while it's out. If the warning starts coming back soon after a full clean, or drying times creep up again with everything clear, that's the point to get it looked at. Is there anything else I can help with?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]

candidates: Blocked plinth filter or heat exchanger behind the bottom front flap (heat-pump/condenser models) (high)
Door fluff filters clogged with fine lint or fabric-softener film, so they look clean but still restrict airflow (medium)
Restricted vent hose (if it is a vented model) (low)
